title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closure on Monday reduces available sales days; similar closures have lowered demand by ~10% in past.

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Past price increases (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) showed no lift; price elasticity suggests ~5% demand drop.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 30.5. No events are scheduled, but the store closes Monday, likely reducing sales. Price increased 3.4% to $5.20, which may suppress demand. Past price hikes (e.g., 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) show no lift, and the noise-adjusted effect of promotions is x1.0. The week after a promotion historically sees x0.83, but no prior promotion occurred. Thanksgiving’s pre-event lift is noise-adjusted to x1.0. The store closure is a known demand reducer. The price increase and closure suggest a downward adjustment. Evidence is limited to one closure and one price change, so shrink toward 1.0. No seasonal ramp in recent weeks.

brief:
PRODUCT: Hot Cocoa Mix | category Grocery | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.20 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.03)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 30.5 | 5%-95%: 1.3 - 49.2 | 10%-90%: 6.3 - 48.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
